summary: The study describes the preparation of high-quality hydrogen-doped indium oxide (In2O3:H) using a low-temperature atomic layer deposition (ALD) process followed by solid-phase crystallization. The process involves depositing amorphous In2O3:H at 100 °C and crystallizing it at 150–200 °C. The resulting films exhibit high carrier mobility and low resistivity, making them suitable for transparent conductive oxide applications, particularly in solar cells.
evidence: The process consists of ALD of amorphous In2O3:H at 100 °C and subsequent solid-phase crystallization at 150 −200 °C to obtain large-grained polycrystalline In2O3:H films. After crystallization, an excellent carrier mobility of 128 ± 4 cm2/(V s) can be obtained at a carrier density of 1.8 × 1020 cm−3, irrespective of the annealing temperature.
